project_overview.name: spring-rest-sakila
project_overview.one_liner: A Spring Boot REST API exposing the MySQL Sakila DVD-rental sample database over HATEOAS/HAL endpoints with JWT security.
project_overview.purpose: Provides a well-structured, secured REST API for CRUD and analytical access to the Sakila sample database (a DVD rental store domain: films, actors, customers, rentals, payments, stores, staff). It serves as a reference implementation showcasing modern Spring Boot practices rather than a production product.
project_overview.description: The application follows a layered, package-by-feature architecture. Each functional domain (auth, catalog, customer, location, payment, rental, staff, store) contains its own controller → service → repository stack plus DTOs, MapStruct mappers, HATEOAS assemblers, and domain converters. Requests are authenticated with a stateless JWT bearer token and authorized via method-level @Secured roles (READ, MANAGE, ADMIN). Simple reads use Spring Data JPA derived queries, while complex projections and joins use QueryDSL and Blaze-Persistence. Responses are HAL representations built by per-resource assemblers. Cross-cutting concerns (global exception handling, MDC logging, caching) live in a common module, and configuration wires persistence, Redis caching, and security. The build (Gradle Kotlin DSL) also generates OpenAPI and Postman artifacts from Spring REST Docs tests.
tech_stack: Gradle (Kotlin DSL), Kotlin kapt annotation processing
layers: repository (Spring Data JPA + QueryDSL/Blaze custom fragments)
domain (entity / dto / mapper / assembler / converter / vo)
key_features: JWT-based stateless authentication with role-based method security (READ/MANAGE/ADMIN)
Full CRUD across 8 domains with consistent HATEOAS/HAL hypermedia responses
Complex/aggregate queries via QueryDSL + Blaze-Persistence (details projections, sales reports)
Redis-backed caching via Spring Cache annotations
Centralized, structured error handling with an ErrorCode contract
Pagination and filtering on collection endpoints
API documentation generated from tests (Spring REST Docs → OpenAPI/Postman)
Observability via Actuator health + Prometheus metrics and MDC logging
project_overview.domain_model_summary: Models the Sakila DVD-rental business: films (with categories, ratings, actors, text) are held in stores' inventory, rented by customers (who have addresses/cities/countries) and served by staff; rentals generate payments. Reference/geographic and enumerated data (category, rating, country, language, special features) are modeled as entities, converters, and constants.

complexity_analysis.summary: The codebase is moderately complex. Individual classes are small, single-responsibility, and highly consistent across domains, which keeps local complexity low. The complexity that exists is concentrated in three areas: the QueryDSL/Blaze-Persistence custom repository implementations, the HATEOAS link-assembly in catalog controllers, and the multi-mechanism persistence configuration. The repetitive per-domain layering inflates file count (~188 main classes) but not conceptual difficulty.

hotspots.reason: QueryDSL + Blaze-Persistence queries with typed projections, multi-table joins, group_concat, and dynamic filters.
Wires three distinct query mechanisms (JPA, raw SQL/MySQL, Blaze) plus criteria factories.
Manual HATEOAS link construction (removeLinks/add/methodOn) across nested actor-film resources.
Large DTO aggregating many nested request/response/filter types.
Rental/return state transitions carry the most genuine business logic.

observations: Strong structural consistency: every domain repeats the same controller/service/repository/DTO/mapper/assembler pattern, so learning one domain generalizes to all.
Complexity is architectural (many collaborating layers/technologies) rather than algorithmic.
Annotation processing (Lombok, MapStruct, QueryDSL Q-classes) hides boilerplate but adds a build-time learning curve.
The interface + *Impl split for services and custom repositories adds indirection typical of enterprise Spring.

noteworthy.title: Weak default JWT signing key
noteworthy.detail: app.jwt.signing-key defaults to a short, hardcoded base64 value in application.yaml. For any real deployment this must be replaced with a strong, externally-managed secret.

noteworthy.title: Database credentials committed in application.yaml
noteworthy.detail: spring.datasource username/password (sakila/sakila) and the Redis password are checked into config. Acceptable for a sample, but should be externalized (env/secret manager) for real use.

noteworthy.title: CSRF and CORS disabled
noteworthy.detail: SecurityFilterConfig disables CSRF and CORS. Reasonable for a stateless bearer-token API, but CORS typically needs an explicit allow-list once a browser client is involved.

noteworthy.title: Consistent layered, package-by-feature design
noteworthy.detail: Each domain mirrors the same controller→service→repository→domain structure with DTOs, MapStruct mappers, and HATEOAS assemblers, making the codebase predictable and easy to extend.

noteworthy.title: Repository composition for complex queries
noteworthy.detail: Spring Data JPA interfaces are composed with QueryDSL/Blaze custom fragments (Custom*Repository + *Impl), cleanly separating derived queries from hand-written ones.

noteworthy.title: Redis-backed caching on hot reads
noteworthy.detail: Service methods use @Cacheable/@CachePut/@CacheEvict (e.g. actorResponseCache) to cache entity reads in Redis.

noteworthy.title: printStackTrace() in the global exception handler
noteworthy.detail: GlobalExceptionHandler calls e.printStackTrace() in addition to SLF4J logging; stack traces should be logged through the logger instead of stdout/stderr.

noteworthy.title: open-in-view enabled
noteworthy.detail: spring.jpa.open-in-view=true keeps the persistence context open for the whole request, which can mask lazy-loading issues and hold connections longer; often disabled in production.

noteworthy.title: show-sql enabled
noteworthy.detail: spring.jpa.show-sql=true logs every SQL statement — useful for a learning project, noisy for production.

noteworthy.title: Docs-as-tests with Spring REST Docs
noteworthy.detail: Controller tests (e.g. ActorControllerTest) drive Spring REST Docs to generate snippets, which the Gradle build turns into OpenAPI and Postman artifacts — API docs stay in sync with tests.

noteworthy.title: Role hierarchy READ < MANAGE < ADMIN
noteworthy.detail: Endpoints are guarded by @Secured with three roles; read operations require ROLE_READ, mutations ROLE_MANAGE, and staff/store administration ROLE_ADMIN.
